header.service: DEMO — UC San Diego Athletics Fan & Revenue Lifecycle
header.scope: First contact with Triton athletics → Renewal, lapse, or a first Triton Athletic Fund gift
header.stages: Awareness → First purchase → Game day → After the game → Renewal or a first gift → Lapse and win-back

steps.step: Awareness — Export purchase history and rebuild the campaign segments
steps.trigger: A campaign is planned, pre-season or in-season
steps.rule: Segments are built by hand; comps are excluded (D-06)
steps.whatGoesWrong: The exported file is roughly a week old by the time the campaign sends, so recent buyers are asked to buy again (FR-02, H-01)

steps.step: Awareness — Choose the segment, the offer, and the send date
steps.rule: The marketer's judgment against prior-season performance; no automated scoring in use
steps.whatGoesWrong: The send lands in the same week as a Fund solicitation, because the two calendars are not shared (FR-08)

steps.step: First purchase — Set the price tier for the game
steps.trigger: Pre-season schedule confirmed; revisited in-season for marquee games
steps.who: Ticket & Event Operations, signed off by the Senior Associate AD (D-01)
steps.rule: The tier recommendation is approved before tickets go on sale
steps.handsOnTime: 2–3 hrs for the season, plus in-season adjustments
steps.whatGoesWrong: Tiers set against last season's draw rather than the new conference slate

steps.step: First purchase — Fan completes the purchase; account and barcode created
steps.rule: An account is created on first purchase
steps.whatGoesWrong: The account record never leaves the ticketing platform; nothing links it to the email platform or to either donor system (FR-01)

steps.step: Game day — Build the comp list and apply the marketing exclusion
steps.rule: Comps do not enter the marketing audience
steps.whatGoesWrong: Exclusions are applied by hand in a spreadsheet, so a comp can reach the audience anyway

steps.step: Game day — Push the manifest and scan attendees in
steps.rule: Every entry scans against a barcode
steps.handsOnTime: ~30 min setup, then the gate window
steps.whatGoesWrong: A transferred ticket scans under the buyer's barcode, so the person who actually attended is never identified (FR-01, FR-03)

steps.step: After the game — Return scan data and send the post-event follow-up
steps.rule: Follow-up is addressed to the account of record
steps.whatGoesWrong: Scan data returns as a gate count, so the follow-up reaches the buyer rather than the people who were there (FR-03, FR-04)

steps.step: Renewal — Issue renewal invoices and send the season-ticket holder file to the Fund
steps.rule: The file is pulled by hand and emailed, roughly once a month
steps.waitTime: Up to a month between pulls
steps.whatGoesWrong: The Fund works from a picture weeks out of date; recent joiners and recent lapses are both missed (FR-05)

steps.step: A first gift — Select who is solicited and at what amount, then request clearance
steps.who: Director, Triton Athletic Fund, with central Advancement (D-04, D-05, H-06)
steps.system: Athletics donor records; central Advancement CRM
steps.rule: Human judgment, no propensity model; an assigned prospect requires central clearance before solicitation
steps.whatGoesWrong: Clearance is requested after the letter has gone out, so an assigned prospect can be solicited without either side knowing (FR-06)

steps.step: A first gift — Process the gift and issue the receipt
steps.rule: Gifts to the Fund are processed and receipted centrally on a batch cycle
steps.whatGoesWrong: The donor calls the Fund about a receipt the Fund cannot produce (FR-07)

steps.step: Lapse and win-back — Build the lapsed list and work it
steps.rule: Worked in spreadsheet order, as far as staff time allows
steps.waitTime: A season, before the lapse is noticed at all
steps.whatGoesWrong: Whether a lapsed buyer is contacted depends on student-worker availability that month rather than on who they were (FR-09)
